question: Should OpenClaw support sandboxed requester sessions spawning ACP by running ACP inside a sandbox, by adding a narrow host-side bridge/proxy, or by folding this into the execution-backend placement contract?
rationale: Changing the current block defines a sandbox-to-host trust boundary plus public config and model-facing tool semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent security design.

options.title: Design Sandbox-Aware ACP Boundary
options.body: Define a narrow bridge or placement contract for ACP spawn, steer, and cancel with explicit auth, audit, workspace, secret, rate-limit, and cleanup rules before implementation.

options.title: Require Harnesses Inside Sandbox
options.body: Keep the host-side ACP block and document installing Claude Code, Codex, or Gemini inside the OpenClaw sandbox container as the supported workflow for now.

options.title: Defer To Execution Backends
options.body: Keep this issue as an acceptance case while the broader execution-backend placement design settles remote-worker and sandbox semantics.

recommendation.title: Design Sandbox-Aware ACP Boundary
recommendation.body: Define a narrow bridge or placement contract for ACP spawn, steer, and cancel with explicit auth, audit, workspace, secret, rate-limit, and cleanup rules before implementation.
